summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell YoY as March 2026 exports stalled on Middle East disruption; consolidated revenue INR 132.1 mn, EBITDA margin 15.74%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year because exports could not be executed in March 2026 after Iran-related conflict disrupted Middle East shipping and logistics. Input costs also rose in March, compressing gross margins. Consolidated revenue was INR 132.1 mn with EBITDA of INR 21.73 mn (15.74% margin) and PAT of INR 5.5 mn (3.97% margin). Management says alternative routes via Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Southeast Asia have restarted shipments and expects a broader export recovery in Q1 FY27. The Pune IV facility, commercial since December 2025, contributed INR 2.7 mn in Q4 versus INR 1.2 mn in Q3.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2.7 mn in Q4 FY26 vs INR 1.2 mn in Q3 FY26

segments.name: Injectables (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 46.7 mn, about 44.43% of revenue from operations.

segments.name: Tablets (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 54.6 mn, about 51.95% of revenue from operations. Management expects tablets and capsules to grow more as dossiers get approved in other countries.

segments.name: IV fluids (Pune, JV/subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Commercial production began December 2025; revenue INR 1.2 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 2.7 cr in Q4 FY26. FY27 target is INR 60-65 cr at 17-18% EBITDA margin; 5 products approved and 18 in pipeline.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals (Prague JV, 45% stake)
segments.commentary: Equity-accounted, so only profit is consolidated, not revenue. Prague business did EUR 0.5-0.6 mn revenue last year; profit could not be remitted in FY26 due to EU first-year dividend restriction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 base business revenue target INR 80-85 cr, with growth of 10-12% from injectables, 7-8% from tablets and 8-9% from nutraceuticals (per management).
FY27 Pune IV revenue target INR 60-65 cr annually; quarterly numbers may vary. Utilisation expected at 40%, 45%, 60% and 70% across the next four quarters.
Base business EBITDA margin guided at 15.5-16.5%.
Pune IV EBITDA margin 17-18% on annualised basis; first two quarters may see margin strain. Management expects breakeven at the IV business in FY27.
Debtor days expected to fall from about 65-70 days to 55-60 days.
Management expects a broader export recovery in Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026).
capex_capacity: Pune IV facility: installed capacity 60 mn bottles annualised; utilisation to ramp from 40% to 70% over the next four quarters.
IV product approvals: 5 approved, 18 in pipeline. Management expects about 6 of the 18 to contribute to the INR 60 cr target; a large chunk of approvals was expected in May 2026.
Pune facility approved and commercialised, but product-wise approvals are an ongoing process that gates scale-up.
Raw material inventory held at about two months.
demand_pricing: Export share 85.26% in Q4 FY26; Latin America, Middle East & Africa and CIS together 76.09% of revenue. Middle East (including Africa) contributes about 40-45% of revenue per management.
No March 2026 exports to the Middle East; new routes via Saudi Arabia and Turkey, and Southeast Asia, now in use, with added logistics cost partly reimbursed by the Government of India.
Pricing is open to international price revisions, with no long-term fixed-price contracts, so input cost increases can be passed on (management cited COVID-era precedent).
Management says import content is under 1% of turnover, but packaging (plastics, aluminium) has been sourced from China and Taiwan after Middle East supply issues.
Competitive positioning cited as quality, turnaround time and customer relationships of 15+ years; named peers Farbe Firma and Kamala Lifesciences.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue decline and how will it accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: March 2026 major shipments were lost to shipping and container disruption tied to the Middle East conflict. Alternate routes are now in use and a fair recovery is expected in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Base business INR 80-85 cr and Pune IV INR 60-65 cr annually, with quarterly figures possibly varying.

qa_highlights.question: Is the base business margin expected to dip given logistics costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no margin dip is expected because a stronger dollar offsets most of the cost pressure; margins expected to stay in line.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables high relative to sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables were INR 11.5 cr on base-business sales of about INR 65 cr, roughly 65 days, down from about 90 days last year. Debtor days are targeted at 55-60.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pune plant's volume and revenue so far?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2 million bottles generated about INR 3.5 cr over Q3 and Q4 FY26, against 60 mn annual capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East disruption continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge could last 1-3 months, with some logistics cost reimbursed by the Government of India.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping disruption and container shortages could persist beyond Q1 FY27; management said the challenge may last 1-3 months.
Pune IV scale-up depends on product-by-product regulatory approvals; 18 pipeline products await approval, with delays due to government process and staff transfers.
Nutraceutical JV profit is not yet being remitted and the majority stake deal is still under negotiation after two years.
Receivables rose sharply versus FY24 and sales growth; collection performance needs tracking against the 55-60 day target.
Crude oil, USD-INR and packaging input costs (plastics, aluminium) remain volatile and could compress margins.
Management did not give a quarterly breakdown for IV revenue, and the INR 10-15 cr quarterly run-rate timeline was not committed to.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident about FY27 and the recovery, giving specific annual targets and margin guidance. It was evasive on quarterly IV run-rate, peer comparisons and the five-year outlook, and it attributed the Q4 shortfall to a one-off March disruption.
key_quotes: So, we have already started the shipments and we expect a fair bit of recovery happening in the Q1 numbers for the current financial year.

Management expects sequential further improvement in the business contribution from the facility during Q1 FY'27 and over the subsequent quarters as additional products get commercialized and scale-up continues.
Going forward on an annualized basis, we expect EBITDA margins of around 17% to 18%.
So, it is, it has improved. So, though entire market is not a cash market or an advanced market.
